name: Plataforma de Contratación del Sector Público (PLACSP)
operator: Dirección General del Patrimonio del Estado, Ministerio de Hacienda
evidenceNote: 2026-08-11: plain curl fails with TLS error 'self signed certificate in certificate chain' (Spanish government CA not in standard trust store) — earlier 'connection failed' reports were this, not a dead site. With chain check bypassed: 200, 97,442 bytes, title 'Plataforma de Contratación del Sector Público'. Search route /wps/portal/licitaciones 200 -> resolves to distinct buscadores/busqueda page, 65,088 bytes, same title. Guides route /wps/portal/guiasAyuda 200, 60,586 bytes, body lists 'Licitación Electrónica' service guides (operator-published e-submission guides, e.g. Guía de Servicios de Licitación Electrónica: Preparación y Presentación de ofertas). Homepage exposes locale=en switch plus Català/Valencià mentions.
limitations: Server certificate chain (Spanish government CA) is not in standard OS trust stores — curl/browsers may need the FNMT/gov CA imported or show warnings
Supplier registration (Empresas > Registrarse) and an electronic certificate are required for e-bidding and notifications; notice search is open without registration

Bid preparation/submission uses the platform's Herramienta de Preparación y Presentación de ofertas behind login — no distinct public submission URL to verify

name: World Bank Group Procurement Notices (Bank-financed project opportunities)
operator: World Bank Group (IBRD/IDA)
evidenceNote: Verified 2026-08-12: curl 200, final URL https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/procurement, 30154 bytes, title 'Procurement Notices'. Page body renders via JS (content area shows 'Loading...' in raw HTML), so listing contents were not observable server-side. Sibling route verified 2026-08-12: https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/opportunities -> 200, 34945 bytes, title 'Business Opportunities' (distinct page, not a redirect to officialUrl). Documentation route verified 2026-08-12: https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/what-we-do/project-procurement/resources -> 200, 56311 bytes, title 'Project Procurement Resources | World Bank Group'. Note that https://www.worldbank.org/en/programs/project-procurement* now 301s to https://www.worldbank.org/ext/en/what-we-do/project-procurement*, so the /ext/ form is canonical.
limitations: Project-financed procurement: this surface publishes opportunities for operations the institution funds but does not itself run. Bids go to the borrower or implementing agency, often on a national system, not to the institution.

DISCOVERY ONLY - NOT A SUBMISSION SYSTEM. This is the World Bank's public notice board for procurement under operations it FINANCES. The Bank does not run these tenders: the Borrower (government ministry, agency or project implementation unit) conducts the procurement and receives the bids, normally on the borrower country's own national e-procurement system, many of which are already covered by Waves T1-T3. Suppliers do not submit World Bank-financed bids to the World Bank.

Notices are generated upstream in STEP (the borrower-facing planning and tracking system) and syndicated here; the public site carries General Procurement Notices, Specific Procurement Notices, Requests for Expressions of Interest and contract award notices.

Bidder eligibility is set by the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers plus the borrower's own bidding documents, not by this website. Eligibility is conditional (eligible-country rules, exclusion of firms under WBG sanctions/debarment, and borrower-specific qualification criteria), so open access to the notice board must not be read as open eligibility to bid.

A second supplier-facing interface over the same corpus exists: SOURCe (source.worldbank.org), an AI conversational front-end. Modelled as part of this record rather than a separate platform - see rejected[].
No supplier account is needed to search or to subscribe to email alerts; there is no registration or submission function on this platform.

Eligibility: Eligibility is governed by the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and by each borrower's bidding documents, not by this portal. Restrictions that commonly apply: the firm's country must be an eligible country, firms under World Bank Group sanction/debarment are excluded, and the borrower may impose national qualification or registration requirements. Free public access to notices is NOT evidence of open bidding eligibility, so recorded as unknown.

Registration portal verified: https://vmp-ext.worldbank.org/ -> 200, 39250 bytes, JS splash-loader shell whose first rendered string is 'Vendor Management Portal'. Public opportunity listing verified: https://www.worldbank.org/en/about/corporate-procurement/business-opportunities/administrative-procurement -> 200, 127753 bytes, title 'Administrative Procurement', listing live solicitations keyed by 'RFxNow <number>' and 'RFP <number>'. Software vendor evidence: https://wbgeprocure.worldbank.org/ -> 200, 4970 bytes, no title; body is a JS redirect handler mapping legacy hosts eprocure-pp-worldbank.synertrade.com and eprocure-pp-worldbank-sso.synertrade.com to the worldbank.org hosts, with app identifier 'ngp420'.
limitations: Corporate procurement: the institution buying for its own account.

This is CORPORATE procurement - the World Bank Group buying for itself. It covers both administrative procurement (goods, services, works for the Bank's own offices) and operational consulting services contracted directly by the Bank. It is NOT the channel for Bank-FINANCED project tenders, which borrowers run.

Registration is a hard gate: a vendor account is required to browse solicitations and to submit. The public listing at the administrative-procurement page shows solicitation titles/numbers but responding requires the RFx Now login.

The official vendors page states 'To become a new World Bank Group Registered Vendor, you must be invited to complete a Vendor Registration form, meet all eligibility requirements, and provide any required supporting documentation.' name: IDB Project Procurement — Procurement Notices, Plans and Awarded Contracts

evidenceNote: Verified 2026-08-12 with full browser headers (plain curl and WebFetch both get Cloudflare 403 'Attention Required!' at 5,483 bytes). officialUrl 200, final URL unchanged, 64,696 bytes, title 'IDB | Procurement for Projects'. tenderSearchUrl 200, 50,883 bytes, title 'IDB | Procurement Notices' — the notice search is a live embedded Microsoft Power BI report (reportId 8a3cf387-d650-401a-8d54-4b3efa166314, workspaceId 7ef88beb-52e4-4082-8230-26a241cea4a5, embedUrl app.powerbi.com/reportEmbed) rendered under tabs 'Open for Bidding Now / Upcoming Processes / Awarded Contracts'. limitations: Project-financed procurement: this surface publishes opportunities for operations the institution funds but does not itself run. Bids go to the borrower or implementing agency, often on a national system, not to the institution.

Discovery surface only — the IDB publishes the notices but does not operate the tender. Class A from the FAQ: 'The borrower is solely responsible for the implementation of the project, including the procurement and payment of goods, works, non-consulting services, and consulting services' and 'Is the IDB a party to procurement contracts? No. Contracts are between the borrower and the supplier, contractor, or consultant. The IDB is not a party to these contracts.'

Bidding documents are obtained from, and bids are submitted to, the borrower's executing agency — frequently on that country's own national e-procurement system (SECOP II, Compras.gov.br, etc., already covered in waves T1-T3), never on an IDB system. Class A: 'Follow the instructions in the notice to obtain the bidding documents directly from the project's executing agency.'

The notice search is a Power BI embed, not a native search or API; the documented filters (country, sector, procurement type, keywords) run client-side inside the report and require a JS-capable browser.
www.iadb.org sits behind Cloudflare and returns 403 to plain curl and to server-side fetchers; browser-like headers (Accept, Accept-Language, Sec-Fetch-*) are required to retrieve HTML.
No IDB supplier account exists for project procurement — there is no registration gate on this surface; qualification happens per-tender with the executing agency.
Coverage is IDB sovereign-guaranteed operations in Latin America and the Caribbean only; IDB Invest (private-sector arm) and IDB Lab operations are out of scope of this database.

Eligibility: Restricted, not open. Eligibility is limited to firms and individuals from the IDB's 48 member countries (26 borrowing LAC members plus non-borrowing members in North America, Europe, Asia and Israel); individual bidding documents may narrow this further ('unless otherwise specified'), and entities sanctioned or cross-debarred by the IDB Group are excluded. Suppliers from non-member countries are not eligible, so this cannot be recorded as foreignSuppliersAccepted=yes.
Part of the Inter-American Development Bank Group ecosystem, which is not modelled as a separate record here.
Supersedes projectprocurement.iadb.org — legacy 'FMP Project Procurement' portal, unreachable and no longer linked from a, which is not published as a record here.

Publication on AFD.dgMarket is mandatory only for international procedures; nationally advertised, below-threshold and locally restricted procedures financed by AFD may never appear here.
Legacy Java stack (.do actions) requiring a session cookie on first hit; a cold request without cookies returns a 240-byte session-bootstrap page.

Eligibility: AFD financing is fully untied, so supplier nationality is not a bar to being financed. Per-tender eligibility, qualification and prequalification conditions are therefore set by the beneficiary contracting authority under local law, and restricted / shortlist procedures are used for intellectual services; AFD's procurement guidelines also exclude sanctioned or debarred entities. foreignEvidenceQuote: All the financing allocated by AFD has been untied since 1 January 2002. Consequently, AFD finances all goods and services, regardless of the country of origin of the supplier or service provider, or the contract amount. This decision not only applies to the least developed countries (LDCs), in line with the OECD recommendation of 20 April 2001, but also to all AFD's partner countries.
